acceptanceCriteria.text: All applicable shipped, runtime-returned and worker-handoff guidance treats the ten-minute mark as an orchestrator progress/stall alarm, not an automatic worker deadline or requirement for a pre-saved exception to continue productive work.

A regression reproducing a productive DM-820-style worker crossing ten minutes shows an evidence-based orchestrator check and continued execution on the same single card/claim, with no clock-only stop, fail, forced epic, Save prerequisite or fresh-attempt reset.

A genuinely stalled worker is investigated and intervention is justified by observed lack of progress or a real blocker; a legitimate long-running operation is not treated as stalled solely because the supervisory alarm fires. Real authorized deadlines, consent/cost limits, safe cleanup and lease fencing remain intact.

Context-selection/push and hosted-handoff regressions demonstrate consistent alarm semantics without depending only on incidental source wording; the required isolated-card verification gate passes with honest evidence. Original task scope, verification gates and human approval controls are not weakened.

body:
## Reported defect and required behavior
The person states that the ten-minute mark is an alarm for the orchestrator to check whether the worker is stuck, NOT a worker cutoff. The orchestrator must investigate progress/stalls and keep productive work running toward the original acceptance criteria. Elapsed time alone must not terminate a worker, fail an attempt, force an epic, or require a fresh claim. File this as one coherent workflow bug; this request is filing only, not permission to launch or implement it.

## Observed reproduction: DM-820
Original card kc_01m7wqy5gw8sqy7p1gavy2s2c1, Always wake message recipients and deliver messages into agent context, on main.
1. A person pressed Play and requested the single card be carried to Ready for review.
2. The orchestrator treated the five/ten-minute guidance as a hard implementation budget, did no implementation in attempt ka_01m7ws4rrehyzbcre1ej9kww12, failed it, and created an unsolicited recovery epic ep_01m7wsbhsrd5gdfnvawr75fcg6. It then incorrectly made saving that epic a prerequisite when the person said to take and work the ticket.
3. The person explicitly rejected an epic and asked to get the single work item done. The orchestrator dispatched one worker under attempt ka_01m7wy7kh3q134096efw0x85vz, but embedded a hard stop deadline in the worker handoff.
4. At five minutes the worker reported real progress: consumer regressions RED then GREEN, full-body delivery code and runtime prerequisites established. No evidence established that the worker was stuck.
5. The worker stopped at the imposed ten-minute deadline despite productive implementation and 48 targeted passing tests. Six files were left uncommitted; c1-c4 were incomplete. The orchestrator failed the attempt rather than supervising continued progress.
6. The person clarified the intended watchdog semantics and explicitly requested this bug ticket.

Evidence records on DM-820: ke_01m7wsgfsdew87ev4j704kh439 (unnecessary decomposition); ke_01m7wy9h1j7efddztybycjkaqd (hard deadline sent to worker); ke_01m7wyj5tw3b1sq4r6ngfstfew (productive five-minute checkpoint); ke_01m7wywcf0qwe64mzje73wbv3f (cutoff and incomplete result). Worker evidence is local://dm820-worker-evidence.json in the reporting chat, not a portable repository artifact. No claim tokens or credentials belong in this record.

## Inspected cause, not just model interpretation
The current shipped knowledge itself instructs the wrong behavior: skills/knowledge/orchestrator/time-box.md calls ten minutes a default deadline and says to stop expansion and fail the attempt at it. time-box-limits.md requires a preclaim saved exception to exceed ten minutes. kanban-run.md imports these rules. skills/planner.md requires all work to fit a 5-10 minute window and forced decomposition before dispatch. These instructions reinforced the observed orchestration failure. Correct all applicable shipped/pushed/pulled/handed-off guidance consistently; changing only an apology or one worker prompt is insufficient. The installed CLI returned even more explicit hard-stop wording during this incident, so verify the bundled runtime context as well as source prose.

## Scope and source locations
- skills/knowledge/orchestrator/time-box.md: replace elapsed-time hard failure with an orchestrator progress/stall alarm, subsequent evidence-based supervision, and explicit continued execution for productive workers.
- skills/knowledge/orchestrator/time-box-limits.md: distinguish supervisory alarm cadence from genuine authorized operation deadlines, consent/cost limits and safe cleanup. Remove the ten-minute saved-exception prerequisite for otherwise productive normal work.
- skills/knowledge/orchestrator/kanban-run.md: ensure single-worker cards use the watchdog semantics, not worker stop/fail or automatic replan.
- skills/orchestrator.md: align supervision, handoffs and blocked/stalled decisions with the corrected behavior.
- skills/planner.md: keep sensible task sizing but remove forced epic/decomposition solely because useful work may exceed an alarm interval; do not turn a person-authorized single card into an unsolicited epic.
- skills/worker.md: inspect/align worker handoff and continuation behavior so workers report progress/questions to the orchestrator, not self-stop solely at the supervisory alarm.
- src/core/knowledge/builtin.test.ts and src/core/knowledge/push.test.ts: existing selection/push regression entry points for the actual claim/recovery and time-box topic payloads.
- src/main/agents/cliInstructions.ts and src/main/agents/cliInstructions.test.ts: inspect generated hosted guidance and any role/handoff text reaching workers, including packaged versus source delivery; change only applicable paths. These are verified entry points, not a claim that this module alone generates the hard-stop text.

## Required supervision semantics
At the alarm, the orchestrator obtains concrete progress/evidence, current operation, expected next result and blockers; it decides whether the worker is progressing, waiting legitimately, or stuck. Progressing workers continue on the same assignment and claim. A worker that appears stuck gets bounded cause-specific investigation/intervention with a recorded reason. No inference that every long operation is stalled; no blind killing, forced fail/restart or forced scope reduction at a clock boundary. Do not eliminate real safety/deadline/consent controls or permit endless unproductive diagnostics. Preserve heartbeat/lease fencing, explicit human approval controls, required tests, full verification and honest incomplete reports for actual failures. Never claim completion merely to avoid another supervision alarm.

## Tests
Add consumer-visible regression scenarios for: (a) a productive worker crossing ten minutes triggers an orchestrator check and continues, without fail or decomposition; (b) a genuinely stalled worker triggers evidence-led diagnosis and an explained intervention; (c) a long-running check within its real authorized deadline is supervised rather than killed by the alarm; (d) a person-requested single card is not blocked on an unsolicited epic Save; (e) emitted claim/recovery/topic and hosted handoff instructions agree on alarm semantics. Exercise actual context selection/rendering/handoff behavior with deterministic clocks/fixtures where testable; do not merely pin incidental source wording. Extend the named existing suites and run targeted tests first; use the required isolated-card delivery gate before implementation is submitted. Filing this card does not run or waive that gate.

## Non-goals
Do not implement DM-820 messaging here, discard its partial changes, automatically delete the unsolicited draft, weaken acceptance, add retries to mask flakes, alter human retry/approval controls, or simply increase the hard cutoff. The fix is watchdog semantics and orchestration behavior, not a longer arbitrary termination timer.
expectedArtifacts: Consistent progress-watchdog guidance in shipped knowledge, role guides and actual runtime/handoff context
Regression coverage for productive, stalled and legitimately long-running workers plus single-card continuation
Verification evidence and incident-linked explanation of the corrected orchestration behavior
title: Treat ten-minute worker checks as progress alarms, not termination deadlines
